story_type: NASA avionics technician rides an F/A-18 over the mountains, cockpit camera
hook: He fixes NASA's jets. Today one tipped him over a mountain ridge.
narration: He keeps NASA's jets working. Today one tipped him on his side over a mountain ridge.
Kelly Jellison is the lead avionics technician for two of NASA's research planes, at Edwards, California.
His reward was the back seat of an F/A-18, with a white bag in his lap, just in case.
The jet left the desert runway and climbed out toward the clouds.
In a steep bank, the wing points at the ground and the pilot pulls the nose around. That is how a fighter turns hard.
Ridge after ridge, the mountains swung past the canopy.
[short pause] Then the jet headed back toward the dry lakebed.
outcome: The F/A-18 landed safely at Edwards, and Kelly Jellison climbed down to a certificate and handshakes.
title: F/A-18 banks hard over a mountain ridge
description:
On May 27, 2026, Kelly Jellison, lead avionics technician for NASA's C-20 and Gulfstream G-V aircraft, rode in the back seat of an F/A-18 at NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, as part of the agency's employee incentive flights.

facts.claim: Kelly Jellison, lead avionics technician for NASA's C-20 and G-V, flew in an F/A-18 at Armstrong in Edwards on May 27, 2026
facts.source_quote: Kelly Jellison, lead avionics technician for NASA's C-20 and Gulfstream G-V aircraft, takes part in an employee incentive flight in an F/A-18 aircraft at NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, on Wednesday, May 27, 2026.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman established the ride-along program to recognize and reward workforce members for their dedication to advancing the agency's priorities.
